newsitem.title: FINLAND: Thin Helsinki up, eyes dollar, earnings and Europe.
newsitem.headline: Thin Helsinki up, eyes dollar, earnings and Europe.

text.p: Shares closed modestly higher on Monday, helped to gains by Nokia as the market shrugged off the French political situation which dragged some European bourses. But trade was exceptionally thin, brokers said.

French financial markets fell amid political uncertainty ahead of an expected snap general election, seen necessary to allow the government to push through austerity measures for France to qualify for a single currency. Nerves spread to London and Frankfurt, which were also weak.
The HEX index closed up 0.54 percent at 2,839.13 after trading in a narrow 2,832.48-2,842.46 range; the FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark closed up 0.49 percent at 991.46.
Brokers said a weaker dollar subdued trade in cyclicals, particularly forestries, which closed flat to lower.
The forestry sub-index fell 0.08 percent but forestry major UPM-Kymmene was flat at 114.50 markka.
Nokia, due to report on Q1 next week, rose 4.00 markka or 1.34 percent to 303.00 markka, making up almost 40 percent of total volume; but brokers said overall sentiment was wary.
"The French snap elections put the whole question of whether EMU will come true back on the agenda, and uncertainty may show in interest rates and eventually on stocks," one broker said.

Swedish Ericsson is due to report first quarter earnings on Friday, giving a hint also about Nokia's progress early this year. Reports from the two leading mobile phone rivals often show the overall market development, but higher market share for one may mean less for the other, analysts say.
Before that another Swedish first quarter report from forestry group Stora, due on Thursday, would be in focus for forestries, brokers said.
